description: We are a team of motivated and creative participants taking part in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge in Zugdidi, Georgia. We are interested in space exploration, science, technology, and innovation. Our goal is to collaborate, share ideas, solve real-world challenges, and develop an innovative project using NASA's open data.
summary: ScoutGrid Mars is an interactive 3D digital twin of Mars built as a single web page for a competition, focused on Jezero Crater and Arcadia Planitia. Travel through time with a slider spanning billions of years, shown in light years, watching the planet change from ancient wet world to the far future. In Mars Walk, you plan routes across a grid map, managing oxygen, battery, radiation, wind storms and hazards. Layers reveal minerals, subsurface ice and surface material. Scouts map unexplored ground and may return or be left behind, while warnings guide risky decisions. A driving mission mode adds exploration.
details:
ScoutGrid Mars is a browser-based digital twin of Mars, covering Jezero Crater, Arcadia Planitia and the route between them. Players travel through time with a slider, then plan routes in Mars Walk while managing oxygen, battery, radiation, storms and hazards. Map layers reveal minerals, ice and surface material. Scouts map unexplored ground: if battery allows, they return; otherwise they’re left behind and must be recovered, with warnings guiding each risky choice.

It teaches students why scouting, resource planning and hazard awareness matter for real Mars missions, and runs on any device with no install.

Built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one file, using Three.js for 3D and canvas for maps and charts.

It’s creative because it blends time travel with survival planning, and the scout dilemma makes players weigh information against risk. We considered realism, safety, accessibility and game balance.
